subject: Urgent: ApexHealth hosted API latency spikes — request backlog & mitigation
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@apexhealth.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Lee <michael.lee@apexhealth.io>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in p95/p99 — production degradation this morning

Jordan —

We started seeing dramatic latency regressions on our production integration with Redwood Hosted API around 09:45 PT. p95 has jumped from ~420ms to ~2.1s and p99 is frequently 6s+. We're also observing occasional 5xx errors (502/504) and a build-up of queued requests on our side. This is impacting clinical ingestion and a few downstream user flows.

Attached is a short CSV with sample latencies and a few span dumps. Can you confirm if there are known issues on your side and advise the immediate mitigation steps? We need a plan we can share with our ops and leadership.

—Sarah
Site Reliability Engineer, ApexHealth
attachments: apex_latency_report_may30.csv, trace_span_samples.txt

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@apexhealth.io>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:28:37 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 — production degradation this morning

Sarah — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments. We’re triaging now. Short answer: we see elevated queue depth and continuous batching windows expanding on the hosted cluster serving the apx-prod model pool which can push p95/p99 up when request rates concentrate.

Immediate steps we’re taking (live):
- Opening an incident in our ND system and paging infra.
- Pulling Datadog traces for the apx-prod routing pool.
- Temporarily reducing batching window to 20ms for apx-prod and prioritizing small payloads.
- Enabling a conservative rate cap on concurrent requests from ApexHealth’s API key to prevent cascading queue buildup.

I’ll follow with a concrete mitigation plan within 30 minutes and keep you posted on rollback criteria. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll aim to minimize impact and provide an RCA after stabilization.

—Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:33:12 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Spike in p95/p99 — production degradation this morning

Looping infra and CS. TL;DR from preliminary checks: sudden traffic burst from one Apex API key + a batch sizing regression on the serving runtime after last night’s kernel selector rollout. We need: (1) emergency policy to reroute to a lower-batching fast path, (2) a short-term quota to smooth the burst, (3) exec visibility in case customer leadership escalates.

Neha — can you run the routing revert (kernel selector) and apply the reduced batching window? Marcus — please prepare a temporary policy to reroute heavy requests to the fast-fallback model instance.

—Sean
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:46:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 — production degradation this morning

Work completed and notes:
- Rolled back last night’s kernel-selector change on the apx-prod pool at 10:40 PT.
- Reduced continuous batching window from 80ms -> 20ms for ApexHealth API key at 10:42 PT.
- Applied a temporary soft concurrency cap per API key (250 concurrent tokens) at 10:44 PT to prevent queue saturation.
- Enabled fast-path routing for < 2k token requests to a quantized fallback model instance.

Initial impact: p95 dropped from ~2.1s -> ~650ms within 10 minutes; p99 from 6s -> ~1.8s. Error rate dropped to baseline but we’re still watching tail latencies and token-heavy requests.

I’ll keep the change window open for 2 hours and monitor. If stable we can make this the new default for the apx-prod pool or introduce a smarter dynamic batching policy.

—Neha
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@apexhealth.io>
Cc: Michael Lee <michael.lee@apexhealth.io>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 11:05:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 — production degradation this morning

Sarah — quick update and next steps for ApexHealth ops: 

What happened: after our initial investigation, a combination of a traffic spike concentrated on your API key and a recent kernel-selector rollout increased batching windows on the apx-prod serving pool. That allowed request backlog to grow and produced elevated p95/p99 and occasional 5xxs.

Immediate remediation we applied (10:40-10:45 PT):
- Reverted the kernel-selector change affecting apx-prod.
- Reduced batching window to 20ms for your key.
- Throttled concurrent requests for your key to prevent queue buildup.
- Routed small payload requests to a quantized fast-fallback model instance.

Observed effect: p95 improved from ~2.1s -> ~650ms, p99 ~6s -> ~1.8s, error rate returned to baseline. We’ve attached the CSV and sample spans for your SRE review.

Planned follow-ups (we propose these with your team):
- Temporary traffic smoothing policy for 24 hours while we harden dynamic batching.
- Postmortem RCA and long-term fix: adaptive batching based on queue depth + priority lanes for critical flows.
- Optional: provision a dedicated pool for ApexHealth (Reserved capacity) to guarantee isolation.

If you prefer, we can set up a short bridge with our infra leads in the next hour.

Thanks for the quick report — we’ll keep monitoring and I’ll escalate to execs if leadership asks for status.

—Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | jordan_blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Michael Lee <michael.lee@apexhealth.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@apexhealth.io>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 11:38:54 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in p95/p99 — production degradation this morning

Thanks for the rapid response. The improvements are visible on our side — ingestion latency is back to acceptable levels for now. A couple asks from leadership:
- Can you provide a short one-pager for our CTO summarizing root cause and immediate mitigation?
- When can you share the RCA timeline and whether a dedicated pool is actionable in the next 30 days?

We’d like an exec-facing note and a scheduled follow-up by EOD Monday.

—Michael
Director of Platform Engineering, ApexHealth

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Exec update & next actions for ApexHealth escalation

Team —

Nice quick containment on this one. Action items before Monday EOD for the exec summary and customer ask: 
1) Jordan: draft a one-page exec summary for ApexHealth CTO — include measurable before/after p95/p99, the immediate mitigation we applied, and our 30-day options (dedicated pool, SLA uplift, or traffic shaping).
2) Neha & Marcus: collaborate on an RCA draft and a concrete timeline for a permanent adaptive batching rollout. Include risk assessment and rollback criteria.
3) Sean: own the conversation re: reserved capacity pricing/ timelines if Apex requests a dedicated pool.

Please copy me on the deliverables and drop the support_plan_v1.docx in this thread when ready. I’ll be available to join the customer call if needed.

—Evelyn
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
